newsitem.title: CHINA: China says stability key goal in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China says stability key goal in 1997.

text.p: China said on Wednesday that social stability would be a priority this year and it called on the Communist rank and file to hold closely to the party line.
"Maintaining social and political stability is a priority in dealing with the overall situation," said a front-page editorial in the People's Daily.

"The whole party should conform to the party central committee politically and ideologically, upholding the central authority and strictly implementing its principles and policies," the official Communist Party newspaper said.
China's leaders see 1997 as a critical period, during which they will regain Hong Kong after 150 years of British rule.
A crucial party congress is also scheduled and major policy guidelines for the years ahead are expected to be mapped out.
China has already begun to tighten ideological controls ahead of the congress, calling for a strengthening of orthodox socialist values.
Many economists have also called for the party's leaders to turn their attention to solving fundamental economic problems, such as reforming inefficient state industry.

Beijing has already said it had won a major battle against inflation last year, cooling the economy and easing pressure on prices. Many economists have argued this gave Beijing the opportunity to address other issues.
But streamlining overstaffed state companies has raised fears that workers thrown out of jobs at big state firms would lead to social unrest.
"Problems must be identified and handled from a political point of view in order to understand the overall relations of reforms, development and stability," the editorial said.
